overall_summary: Crypto remains under pressure as escalating geopolitical conflicts and hawkish Fed signals fuel a broad risk-off move. Bitcoin rebounded above sixty thousand on heavy whale buying after liquidations, yet ETF outflows and miner selling risks keep the tone cautious. Markets now eye Wednesday's PCE and GDP data with the dollar elevated and a December hike nearly priced in.
key_points: Geopolitical escalations spark sharp risk-off tone
Whales buy over one billion Bitcoin dip
Spot Bitcoin ETFs see heavy November outflows
Fed hike odds near-certain, dollar near highs
Key PCE inflation and GDP data due Wednesday

items.title: Bitcoin crashes to two-year low then rebounds above $60k
items.summary: Bitcoin slid to roughly fifty-five thousand one hundred thirty dollars on Saturday, its weakest level since September twenty twenty-four, as AI stock weakness and risk-off macro pressure hit crypto. Buyers stepped in hard and price reclaimed the sixty thousand area with gains of five to nine percent in twenty-four hours. Traders should care because this tests whether the multi-year low holds as a floor after a sharp weekly drawdown of around eight to fourteen percent. The bounce calmed panic selling but leaves Bitcoin still well below key longer-term averages.
items.impact: Short-term relief rally and potential base if sixty thousand holds

items.title: Over one point five billion dollars liquidated in crypto wipeout
items.summary: Roughly one point five to two point seven billion dollars in leveraged positions were liquidated across exchanges in twenty-four hours, hitting more than two hundred sixty thousand traders. Longs took the bulk of the damage on the way down to the fifty-five thousand low, then shorts got squeezed for tens of millions as price bounced. This clears a large chunk of crowded leverage and often precedes calmer or higher price action once forced sellers are gone. Watch open interest and funding for signs the flush is complete.
items.impact: Leverage reset that can support a bounce but does not guarantee trend change

items.title: Abraxas Capital and whales buy over one billion in Bitcoin dip
items.summary: On-chain trackers report Abraxas Capital withdrew about seventeen thousand five hundred ninety-seven Bitcoin worth roughly one point zero four billion dollars from Binance and Kraken while price traded below sixty thousand, averaging near fifty-nine thousand two hundred. Other large players also moved stablecoins and accumulated. This is notable institutional-scale dip buying that reduced exchange supply and may have helped fuel the rebound. Traders should watch whether similar smart-money flows continue or reverse.
items.impact: Supports the bounce and signals larger players accumulating at lower levels

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs bleed five hundred eighty-two million, November near three point five billion outflows
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about five hundred eighty-two million dollars in net outflows on November nineteenth, with BlackRock IBIT alone at five hundred forty-one million, one of its largest days. November totals reached roughly three point four to three point five billion dollars in redemptions across multiple sessions. This shows persistent institutional and retail selling pressure even as price bounced over the weekend. Continued outflows would cap upside until flows stabilize or turn positive.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure that may limit the durability of any rebound

items.title: Kraken BTC CAD pair flashes to seventeen thousand equivalent, trades stand
items.summary: Bitcoin on Kraken’s Canadian-dollar pairs briefly traded as low as about twenty-four thousand two hundred fifty Canadian dollars, roughly sixteen thousand nine hundred to seventeen thousand US dollars, while the USD pair stayed near fifty-seven to fifty-eight thousand. Kraken said systems processed orders correctly, found no breach, and all executed trades will stand. This was a local liquidity dislocation rather than a market-wide crash, but it highlights thin books and execution risk on regional pairs during stress. Bargain hunters keep fills; sellers eat the losses.
items.impact: Isolated exchange event with limited broader price impact but raises liquidity concerns

items.title: JPMorgan: Bitcoin far below eighty-six thousand mining cost, miners may sell
items.summary: JPMorgan analysts put Bitcoin production cost near eighty-six thousand dollars, leaving a gap of more than twenty-six thousand dollars after the drop below sixty thousand. They say higher-cost miners are likely selling reserves to cover operations or fund AI pivots. This adds potential supply overhang on top of ETF outflows. If unprofitable miners shut down, hashrate and difficulty could adjust lower over time, but near-term selling remains a headwind.
items.impact: Increased miner selling pressure that can weigh on price recovery

items.title: Key PCE Inflation and GDP Data Due Wednesday
items.summary: No major US economic releases hit today on Sunday, but Wednesday November 25 brings the second estimate of third-quarter GDP and the October Core PCE price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. This is the last major inflation reading before the December FOMC meeting. Traders should care because a hot print could lock in more hawkish pricing and pressure risk assets including Bitcoin, while a cooler one might ease rate-hike fears.
items.impact: High volatility catalyst for rates, dollar and crypto ahead of Dec FOMC

items.title: Fed's Cook Pushes for More Rate Hikes on Inflation
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said Friday the current policy rate is not high enough and more hikes are needed because inflation remains too high and is not easing. She was one of the two dissenters who wanted a hike in October. Crypto traders should watch this as it reinforces the hawkish consensus heading into December, raising the odds of tighter financial conditions that typically weigh on Bitcoin.
items.impact: Supports higher-for-longer rates, negative for risk assets

items.title: Dollar Index Holds Near 19-Month Highs Around 104
items.summary: The US Dollar Index closed the week near 103.8 to 103.9, marking a fourth straight weekly gain and hovering close to its highest level since April 2025. Strength came from firm Fed hike expectations even as the rally stalled slightly on Friday. A strong dollar tends to tighten global liquidity and act as a headwind for Bitcoin and other risk assets.
items.impact: Dollar strength pressures crypto and emerging-market flows

items.title: Treasury Yields Drop Sharply on Risk-Off Flight
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 10 basis points on Friday to around 4.91 percent, one of its biggest daily drops recently, as investors fled tech and AI-related stocks into bonds. The 2-year also declined even while December hike odds stayed high. Lower yields can support risk assets short-term, but the move reflects equity fear rather than a full dovish pivot.
items.impact: Temporary relief for duration-sensitive assets if yields stabilize lower

items.title: Markets Price Near-Certain 25bp Fed Hike in December
items.summary: Fed funds futures continue to show roughly 90 to 95 percent odds of a quarter-point rate increase at the December 8-9 FOMC meeting, with only slim chances of a larger 50 basis point move. Recent minutes and speeches from multiple officials back further tightening. This keeps financial conditions relatively tight and caps upside for Bitcoin until the path becomes clearer.
items.impact: Entrenches higher rates outlook, limiting crypto liquidity

items.title: UMich Sentiment Rises, Inflation Expectations Fall
items.summary: The final University of Michigan consumer sentiment index for November was revised up to 51.5 from 48.0 in October, its highest in three months, while one-year inflation expectations dropped sharply to 3.7 percent from 4.7 percent. The improvement came partly from post-election optimism and lower gas prices. Softening inflation expectations could give the Fed slightly more room, though absolute levels remain elevated.
items.impact: Mildly supportive if it softens longer-term rate fears

items.title: Iran Strikes US Bases in Bahrain; Tankers Hit in Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched missile and drone attacks on US military positions in Bahrain, claiming hits on Patriot radars, while Bahrain reported a fire at a civilian industrial site with no casualties. At the same time, multiple oil tankers were struck by projectiles or mines in the Strait of Hormuz. This keeps the nearly nine-month US-Iran conflict hot and threatens the key oil chokepoint. Traders should care because any further disruption to Gulf crude flows can spike energy prices and trigger broad risk-off moves across crypto and equities.
items.impact: Higher oil prices and elevated geopolitical risk premium pressure risk assets

items.title: Russian Missiles Enter Poland; NATO Pledges Full Defense
items.summary: During a massive Russian barrage on Ukraine, cruise missiles and a drone crashed in southeastern Poland, a NATO member. Polish leaders called it an intentional provocation timed with allied exercises, and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte vowed the alliance will defend every inch of Polish territory. This follows heavy strikes that also hit Zelensky's hometown. For markets, any credible risk of direct NATO-Russia confrontation is a classic risk-off catalyst that can slam Bitcoin and other high-beta assets.
items.impact: Heightened NATO-Russia escalation fears drive flight to safety

items.title: Ukrainian Drone Hits Russian Military Ship in Baltic Sea
items.summary: A Russian cargo vessel linked to military logistics, the Sparta II bound for Kaliningrad, was struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland, caught fire, and drifted into Finnish waters. Finland said Ukraine was likely responsible and noted the war is spilling into NATO's immediate neighborhood. Crew was evacuated safely. This expands the conflict's footprint into the Baltic and raises odds of further incidents near NATO states, adding another layer of uncertainty for global risk markets.
items.impact: War spillover into NATO waters increases systemic geopolitical risk

items.title: Trump Pushes Ukraine Peace Deal Before January Congress Shift
items.summary: The Trump administration is urgently pressing Ukraine and Russia for a peace agreement by early January, before Democrats take control of Congress after the midterms. US envoys have been shuttling between capitals conveying the deadline, while Kyiv and European officials worry it could force major Ukrainian concessions. A credible deal would remove a major overhang, but a rushed or unfavorable one could prolong instability. Crypto traders should watch closely as resolution or collapse of talks can swing risk sentiment sharply.
items.impact: Unresolved peace push creates event-driven volatility for risk assets

items.title: Houthis Fire Missiles at Riyadh as Saudi Conflict Escalates
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis launched ballistic missiles toward the Saudi capital Riyadh, which the Saudi-led coalition intercepted, marking continued cross-border attacks after earlier damage to a major Riyadh tower housing the sovereign wealth fund. The group also threatened ports and airspace. This secondary Middle East front compounds energy security worries already driven by the Iran conflict. Sustained attacks on Saudi infrastructure keep a risk premium in oil and can spill into broader market caution.
items.impact: Additional Gulf energy infrastructure threats support higher oil and risk-off tone

items.title: COP31 Climate Talks Deadlocked Over Fossil Fuels
items.summary: UN climate negotiations in Turkey have entered a second day of overtime with deep divisions over any language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, opposed by Saudi Arabia and other producers. A new draft recalls prior commitments but avoids explicit phase-out wording, raising the chance of no deal. While not an immediate black swan, failure or a weak outcome reinforces the status quo for oil and gas supply. Energy traders and risk assets may see limited direct impact but watch for any signal on long-term fossil demand policy.
items.impact: Policy uncertainty for energy transition; limited near-term market move
